label: Supplier connection locks
purpose: How often hotel supplier API connections were locked (temporarily blocked) by lock rules after too many errors or time-outs. Also gives the rule that fired and its error threshold and timing settings.
grain: One lock occurrence: a lock rule blocking a supplier connection (credential), dated by lock day and hour.
use_for: supplier connection locks by supplier, credential or lock rule
lock trends by day, week, month or hour of day
which lock rules and error thresholds fire most
distinct locks compared with lock occurrences
not_for: hotel locks in the booking flow, where a hotel option failed for a customer (History Hotel Locks)
supplier request volumes, errors or time-outs (Statistics Supplier Error API Hotel)
customer, market or channel analysis: about 97% of locks have no customer

coverage.note: Sparse before mid-2025: about 1,500 locks in all from March 2023 to May 2025, with several empty months. Regular volumes (about 1,000 to 3,000 a month) start in July 2025, so trends and year-on-year comparisons are meaningful only from then.

dates.label: Lock date
dates.meaning: Day the supplier connection was locked (the cube's only day-level date).

measures.name: [Locked Times]
measures.label: Lock occurrences
measures.definition: Number of times a supplier connection was locked by a lock rule.
measures.notes: Main measure (measure group 'Locks'). The cube gives it no format. 29,707 locks all-time, 22,520 in the last 12 months.

measures.name: [Locks]
measures.label: Distinct locks
measures.definition: Distinct count of locks: a lock that appears in several rows counts once.
measures.notes: Measure group 'Distinct Locks'. Never add it across rows or periods; query the total directly. 20,635 distinct locks against 29,707 occurrences all-time. What makes a lock distinct is not documented.

breakdowns.label: Supplier
breakdowns.meaning: Hotel supplier whose connection was locked.

breakdowns.label: Supplier code
breakdowns.meaning: Short code of the supplier.

breakdowns.label: Supplier credential
breakdowns.meaning: Supplier connection account (credential) that was locked.

breakdowns.label: Lock rule
breakdowns.meaning: Lock rule that fired. The name usually gives the supplier and the kind of failure it watches (performance errors or time-outs).

breakdowns.label: Rule active
breakdowns.meaning: Whether the lock rule is active.

breakdowns.label: Error limit
breakdowns.meaning: Error-rate threshold that triggered the lock. It appears to be recorded with each lock.

breakdowns.label: Rule error limit (rule setting)
breakdowns.meaning: Error limit as set on the lock rule. It does not match 'Errors Limit'[Errors Limit] (it has no 50% value and has different counts), so it is probably the rule's current setting. Hidden in favour of the lock-level column.

breakdowns.label: Max errors
breakdowns.meaning: Number of errors allowed before the connection is locked.

breakdowns.label: Error window (seconds)
breakdowns.meaning: Window, in seconds, over which errors are counted for the rule.

breakdowns.label: Lock duration (seconds)
breakdowns.meaning: How long, in seconds, the rule keeps the connection locked.

breakdowns.label: Request type
breakdowns.meaning: Type of request that was locked.

breakdowns.label: Sale channel
breakdowns.meaning: Sale channel of the customer linked to the lock. About 97% are 'Unknown'; the only other value with data is XML.

breakdowns.label: Customer
breakdowns.meaning: Customer linked to the lock. About 97% of locks are 'Unknown'.

breakdowns.label: Master agency code
breakdowns.meaning: Master agency code: the only key that links these customers to other cubes, and only partly.

breakdowns.label: Market
breakdowns.meaning: Market of the customer linked to the lock. About 97% of locks are 'Unknown'.
sample_values: GCC - Except UAE and Local Residence

breakdowns.label: Year
breakdowns.meaning: Year of the lock (number).

breakdowns.label: Quarter
breakdowns.meaning: Quarter, written "Quarter 1, 2026".

breakdowns.label: Month
breakdowns.meaning: Month, written "November 2025".

breakdowns.label: Week
breakdowns.meaning: Week with its year, written "51 (2025)".

breakdowns.meaning: Day of the week (Monday to Sunday).

breakdowns.label: Hour of day
breakdowns.meaning: Hour of the lock, "00" to "23".

named_filters.meaning: Locks fired by rules that are active.

named_filters.name: inactive lock rules
named_filters.meaning: Locks fired by rules that are now inactive.

rules: These are supplier connection locks: a lock rule blocked a supplier connection for a while after too many errors or time-outs. They are not "hotel locks" (History Hotel Locks: a hotel option failed for a customer in the booking flow). Never answer a "hotel locks" question from this cube, nor a "supplier locks" question from History Hotel Locks.
[Locks] is a distinct count: never add it across rows, months or cubes. Use [Locked Times] for totals and shares.
Customer, market and channel are 'Unknown' for about 97% of locks. Customers match other cubes only by master agency code, and only partly: do not compare customers across cubes from this cube.
Data is sparse before July 2025. Do not read trends or year-on-year changes from earlier periods.
Use the 'Errors Limit', 'Max Errors' and 'Recollection Times' tables for the thresholds behind a lock. The same-named 'Lock Rules' columns hold the rule's settings and do not match.
'Locked Minutes' and 'Lock Rules'[Credential Name] have no usable data, and 'Lock Rules'[Request Type] is always Availability. Week Of Year has no year, so use 'Locked Date'[Week Year].

review.question: Does "how many supplier locks" mean lock occurrences or distinct locks?
review.why: It is the cube's main measure and adds up across suppliers, months and rules. [Locks] is a distinct count (about 30% lower) and cannot be summed.

review.question: For "error limit" or threshold questions, should we use the lock-level 'Errors Limit' table or the rule's 'Lock Rules'[Errors Limit]?
review.why: The two disagree (only the lock-level column has 50%, and the counts per value differ). The lock-level one appears to record the threshold in force when the lock happened.

review.question: When someone says just "hotel locks", do they mean booking-flow hotel locks or supplier connection locks?
options: Supplier Lock API Hotel (supplier connection locks)
review.why: That cube is literally about hotel locks. This cube is used only for "supplier locks", "supplier connection locks" or "supplier API locks".
